questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, what should motorcycle riders be careful of?

options.text: Drivers looking for a parking space.
Cars pulling out of parking spaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars pulling out of parking spaces.
questions.explanation: When passing parked vehicles, be careful. A car may pull out of a parking space or away from the curb without warning.

questions.question: When braking, which brakes should you use?

options.text: Either brake, but never both at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes at the same time to stop. The brakes work best when you use them together.

questions.question: What is the best gear to wear when riding?

options.text: Any gear that helps protect you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any gear that helps protect you.
questions.explanation: Wear gear that protects you while riding. This includes a DOT-approved helmet, eye protection, and protective clothing.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a bridge grating?

options.text: Ride on the far right side of the lane.
Ride on the far left side of the lane.
Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Bridge gratings may cause your motorcycle to weave. This is normal and not dangerous. Stay relaxed and keep a steady speed going straight across. Zigzagging is dangerous because it forces you out of your lane.

questions.question: What is the most important thing you can do to survive a crash?

options.text: Wear a good helmet that is fastened securely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a good helmet that is fastened securely.
questions.explanation: Wearing a good helmet that is fastened securely is the single best thing you can do to survive a crash.

questions.question: What is important about the clothing you wear when riding?

options.text: It should be loose enough to flap in the wind.
It should not cover your arms or legs completely.
You should not wear a jacket in warm weather.
It can protect you in a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can protect you in a crash.
questions.explanation: Good clothing provides important protection in a crash. Always wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs, even in warm weather. Your clothing should fit snugly so it does not flap, but loose enough to move freely.

questions.question: What happens when you drink alcohol quickly?

options.text: Alcohol builds up in your body.
The effects of alcohol are less.
You are more likely to avoid being pulled over.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: When you drink quickly, alcohol builds up in your body. Never ride a motorcycle after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: Is the front brake safe to use?

options.text: Only if the rear brake fails.
No, do not use it regularly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if used correctly.
questions.explanation: The front brake is safe when used correctly. It is more powerful than the rear brake and provides most of your stopping power.

questions.question: What should you do when you cannot avoid an obstacle or uneven surface?

options.text: Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Rise slightly off the seat so your legs absorb the impact.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rise slightly off the seat so your legs absorb the impact.
questions.explanation: Approach at a 90-degree angle if possible. Slow down as much as you can. Keep the motorcycle upright. Rise slightly off the seat so your legs can absorb some of the impact. Just before hitting the obstacle, roll on the throttle a little to lighten the front end.

questions.question: Where is the throttle on a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handle grip.
questions.explanation: The throttle is on the right handle grip. Know where all your motorcycle's controls are before you ride.

questions.question: When doing a pre-ride check, make sure that:

options.text: The brakes make a loud squeaking sound.
The brakes rub against the steering.
Each brake can hold the motorcycle.
Only the rear brake can hold the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each brake can hold the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Check each brake lever before every ride. Make sure each one feels firm and stops the motorcycle when you pull it all the way.

questions.question: Shifting to a lower gear is similar to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Braking.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have a manual transmission. When you downshift to a lower gear, it will slow you down.

questions.question: Turn signals on a motorcycle:

options.text: Do not matter much since motorcycles are smaller than other vehicles.
Are very important to warn other drivers about your plans.
Should not be used if no vehicles are near you.
Are harder to use than signals on a car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are very important to warn other drivers about your plans.
questions.explanation: You are at risk as a motorcycle rider. Always use turn signals to tell others what you plan to do. Use them every time you turn or change lanes, even if you think no one is nearby.

questions.question: What is the best footwear for a motorcycle rider?
questions.correctAnswerText: Sturdy boots
questions.explanation: Sturdy boots or high shoes that support your ankles give the best protection. Laced boots are best. If your boots have long laces, tie them up tightly before riding so they do not get caught.

questions.question: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) are designed to:

options.text: Stop the wheels from sliding and locking.
Stop brakes from working on dry roads.
Apply brakes without the rider touching them.
Tell you when brake pads need to be replaced.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the wheels from sliding and locking.
questions.explanation: Some motorcycles have ABS. It stops the wheels from sliding and locking when you brake hard in a straight line. When sensors detect a wheel about to lock, ABS releases and reapplies the brakes to keep maximum stopping power.

questions.question: If a car is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Move to the side to let them share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may make it worse by letting them tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: Before riding, check your tires for all of the following except:
questions.correctAnswerText: How shiny they are
questions.explanation: Before each ride, check your tire air pressure, tread, and wear.

questions.question: If you have been drinking and wait one hour per drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
You may still have side effects from the alcohol.
You will be fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may still have side effects from the alcohol.
questions.explanation: The body gets rid of about one drink per hour. But alcohol can still build up in your body. Your abilities and judgment can still be hurt.

questions.question: For the best protection, riding gloves should be made of:
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather.
questions.explanation: Gloves should be made of leather or another strong material to give you good protection.

questions.question: Low-speed crashes:

options.text: Happen all the time, so you do not need to worry.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be fatal.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen at speeds below 30 miles per hour. Even low-speed crashes can kill you.

questions.question: Riding gloves are usually made of:
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riding gloves are usually made of leather. They improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders should wear shoes with soles that are:
questions.correctAnswerText: Hard, durable, and slip-resistant.
questions.explanation: Choose boots or shoes that are high and sturdy to cover and support your ankles. The soles should be hard, durable, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: Proper motorcycle riding clothes should:

options.text: Fully cover your arms and legs.
Cover your arms but leave your legs exposed.
Cover your legs but leave your arms exposed.
Be whatever feels most comfortable, no matter the safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fully cover your arms and legs.
questions.explanation: For proper protection while riding, wear a jacket and pants that fully cover your arms and legs.

questions.question: If your motorcycle's chain or belt breaks, you will:

options.text: Feel a sudden increase in power to the rear wheel.
Feel a sudden loss of power to the rear wheel.
Feel a sudden loss of power to the front wheel.
Feel a sudden increase in power to the front wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Feel a sudden loss of power to the rear wheel.
questions.explanation: If your chain or belt fails, power to the rear wheel will stop immediately.

questions.question: When you are about to turn, you:

options.text: Do not need to use a turn signal.
Should always use a turn signal.
Only need a turn signal if pedestrians are nearby.
Only need a turn signal at a stop light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should always use a turn signal.
questions.explanation: Always use a turn signal every time you turn or change lanes, even if your intentions seem obvious. Other vehicles may be nearby that you cannot see.

questions.question: Alcohol impairment:

options.text: Starts at about half the legal limit.
Happens only at the legal limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Starts with the first drink.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your ability to ride safely. You can be impaired before reaching the legal alcohol limit. No amount of alcohol is safe before riding.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, you should be ready for:

options.text: A car to suddenly pull out into traffic.
Other drivers to see you and stay out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: A car to suddenly pull out into traffic.
questions.explanation: A parked car may suddenly pull into traffic. Ride in the left part of your lane when passing parked cars on your right. This gives you more space from possible dangers.

questions.question: A DOT-approved helmet:

options.text: Can greatly reduce head injury severity.
Makes it harder to control your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can greatly reduce head injury severity.
questions.explanation: A helmet greatly improves your chances of avoiding serious head or neck injury in a crash. A DOT-approved helmet will not block your side vision.

questions.question: If you are riding in another vehicle's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Stay where you are to avoid surprising the driver.
Wave at the driver to get their attention.
Slow down to get out of the blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to get out of the blind spot.
questions.explanation: If you are in a vehicle's blind spot, speed up quickly or slow down to move out of it.
